Eines der rötesten Objekte im Sonnensyst: One of the reddest objects in the solar system on an extremely elongated orbit: At perihelion (around 2076) Sedna is 76 AU away, at aphelion almost 1,000 AU. One orbit takes over 11,000 years. How Sedna got onto this orbit is unresolved – perhaps by a passing star.
Der Mond entstand vermutlich, als vor 4,: The Moon probably formed when a Mars-sized body (Theia) collided with the young Earth 4.5 billion years ago. The dark "seas" are solidified lava. It moves away from the Earth by 3.8 cm every year. Twelve people walked on it between 1969 and 1972.
Phobos kreist so dicht über dem Mars, da: Phobos orbits so closely over Mars that it orbits faster than Mars rotates – it rises in the west. Tidal forces are slowly pulling it down: In about 50 million years, it will break apart or crash. The Stickney crater is almost half as large as the moon itself.
Der kleinere Marsmond ist mit Staub (Reg: The smaller Martian moon is covered with dust (regolith), which smooths its craters. From Mars, it would only look like a bright star.
Der vulkanisch aktivste Körper des Sonne: The most volcanically active body in the solar system: Over 400 active volcanoes eject sulfur up to 500 km high. The energy comes from tidal friction – Jupiter, Europa, and Ganymede constantly knead Io, and the surface rises and falls by up to 100 m.
Unter Europas 15–25 km dicker Eiskruste: Beneath Europa's 15–25 km thick ice crust lies a global ocean with more water than all the seas of Earth. The reddish-brown cracks (Lineae) occur when tides break the ice. Europa is considered one of the most promising places for extraterrestrial life; the Europa Clipper probe is on its way.
Der größte Mond des Sonnensystems – größ: The largest moon of the solar system – larger than the planet Mercury. As the only moon, Ganymede has its own magnetic field; it produces auroras. Dark, old regions alternate with bright, furrowed ice.
Die am dichtesten mit Kratern übersäte O: The most densely cratered surface in the solar system – almost unchanged for 4 billion years. The Valhalla impact left rings with a diameter of 3,800 km.
Einer der rötesten Körper des Sonnensyst: One of the reddest bodies in the solar system, an elongated chunk within the orbit of Io. Its dust feeds Jupiter's fine gossamer ring.
Der größte der äußeren, unregelmäßigen J: The largest of the outer, irregular Jovian moons – probably a captured asteroid.
Der „Todesstern“-Mond: Der Krater Hersch: The "Death Star" moon: The Herschel crater is one-third as large as Mimas itself. Mimas clears the Cassini division in Saturn's rings with its gravity.
Der hellste Körper des Sonnensystems. Au: The brightest body in the solar system. From the "tiger stripes" at the south pole, fountains of water vapor and ice shoot into space – supply for Saturn's E-ring. Cassini flew through the fountains and found salt, silicates, and organic molecules from an underground ocean.
Fast reines Wassereis. Der Einschlagkrat: Almost pure water ice. The Odysseus impact crater and the 2,000 km long Ithaca Chasma graben characterize it.
Auf der Rückseite ziehen sich helle Eisk: On the far side, bright ice cliffs stretch for hundreds of kilometers – fracture edges, no deposits, as Cassini showed.
Saturns zweitgrößter Mond, eine kalte, k: Saturn's second-largest moon, a cold, crater-scarred ice ball with bright fracture zones.
Ein schwammartiger Brocken mit sehr geri: A spongy chunk with very low density that tumbles chaotically – its rotation is unpredictable.
Ein Flickenteppich aus völlig verschiede: A patchwork of completely different landscapes with the highest cliff in the solar system: Verona Rupes, around 20 km deep.
Der hellste Uranusmond mit jungen Graben: The brightest Uranus moon with young grabens and smooth plains.
Der dunkelste der großen Uranusmonde, al: The darkest of the large Uranus moons, old and crater-scarred; a bright ring (Wunda) shines at the edge.
Der größte Uranusmond mit riesigen Canyo: The largest Uranus moon with giant canyons that testify to the expansion of the freezing interior.
Der äußerste große Uranusmond: alt, dunk: The outermost large Uranus moon: old, dark, with craters whose floors are covered by dark material.
Einer der größten unregelmäßig geformten: One of the largest irregularly shaped moons – just small enough not to have collapsed into a sphere.
Hat eine der exzentrischsten Mondbahnen:: Has one of the most eccentric moon orbits: The distance to Neptune fluctuates between 1.4 and 9.7 million km.
Eris' dunkler Begleiter; aus seiner Bahn: Eris' dark companion; its mass was determined from its orbit.
Der hellste Asteroid – manchmal mit bloß: The brightest asteroid – sometimes visible to the naked eye. At the south pole lies the Rheasilvia impact crater, 505 km wide with a 22 km high central peak. The HED meteorites found on Earth originate from this impact.
Der drittgrößte Asteroid auf einer stark: The third largest asteroid on a highly inclined orbit (35°) – difficult to reach, therefore never visited.
Fast rund – vielleicht ein Kandidat für: Almost round – perhaps a candidate for the smallest dwarf planet.
2001 setzte die Sonde NEAR Shoemaker hie: In 2001, the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft landed here as the first spacecraft ever to land on an asteroid.
Ein lockerer Schutthaufen in Kreiselform: A loose pile of rubble in a tumbler shape. OSIRIS-REx collected samples in 2020, which landed on Earth in 2023 – containing amino acids and phosphates.
Am 13. April 2029 rast Apophis in nur 32: On April 13, 2029, Apophis will fly past Earth at an altitude of only 32,000 km – lower than geostationary satellites and visible to the naked eye. An impact is ruled out for the next 100 years.
Das fernste je besuchte Objekt (New Hori: The farthest ever visited object (New Horizons, 2019): two gently merged lumps, untouched since the formation of the solar system.
Der berühmteste Komet kehrt alle 75–76 J: The most famous comet returns every 75–76 years; it was already observed in 240 BC. In 1986, the Giotto spacecraft flew as close as 600 km to the nucleus. Its dust produces meteor showers twice a year: the Eta Aquariids in May and the Orionids in October.
Der Komet mit der kürzesten bekannten Um: The comet with the shortest known orbit of a larger comet: 3.3 years. It is the source of the Taurid meteor shower.
Der größte Körper, der regelmäßig nahe a: The largest body that regularly passes close to Earth's orbit. Every August, Earth crosses its dust trail – the Perseids. Next perihelion: 2126.
Seine Staubspur erzeugt im November die: Its dust trail produces the Leonids in November – in 1833 and 1966, up to 100,000 meteors per hour fell.
Flog 2015 an Pluto und 2019 an Arrokoth: Flew past Pluto in 2015 and Arrokoth in 2019 and continues to explore the Kuiper Belt.
Der reichste Strom des Jahres, Mitte Dez: The richest shower of the year, in mid-December – and the only one originating from an asteroid.
Langsame, oft helle Feuerkugeln im Oktob: Slow, often bright fireballs in October and November from the broad dust stream of Encke.

Saturns Ringe sind 280 000 km breit, abe: Saturn's rings are 280,000 km wide, but mostly only 10 to 100 meters thick – they consist of billions of ice chunks ranging from dust grain to house size. The planet has the lowest density of all: it would float in a giant bathtub. At the North Pole, a hexagonal cyclone rotates.
Kommandokapsel Columbia und Mondfähre Ea: Command module Columbia and lunar module Eagle: the first manned Moon landing. You can find the mission under “Missions”.
Die Mondlandung, die zur Rettungsmission: The Moon landing that became a rescue mission. You can find the mission under “Missions”.

Rover im Jezero-Krater mit dem Hubschrau: Rover in the Jezero Crater with the Ingenuity helicopter. You can find the mission under “Missions”.
Die erste bemannte Mondlandung: Neil Arm: The first manned Moon landing: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed with the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility, Michael Collins remained in the Columbia command capsule in Moon orbit. The path here follows the crew.
Die 110 m hohe Saturn V steht auf Startr: The 110 m tall Saturn V stands on launch pad 39A at the Kennedy Space Center. It remains one of the most powerful rockets ever flown.
13:32 UTC: Die fünf F-1-Triebwerke der e: 13:32 UTC: The five F-1 engines of the first stage burn 13 tons of fuel per second. After 12 minutes, Apollo 11 is in orbit.
In 190 km Höhe umkreist das Raumschiff d: At an altitude of 190 km, the spacecraft orbits the Earth in 88 minutes. The crew checks all systems before heading to the Moon.
Die dritte Stufe zündet ein zweites Mal: The third stage fires a second time for 6 minutes: from 7.8 to 10.8 km/s. This is almost enough to leave the Earth – the orbit is a long ellipse whose far end crosses the Moon.
Drei Tage Freiflug. Die Erdanziehung bre: Three days of free flight. Earth's gravity slows down the spacecraft – at halfway, it is only about 1 km/s fast. Only near the Moon does its gravity pull again.
Hinter dem Mond, ohne Funkkontakt zur Er: Behind the Moon, without radio contact to Earth, the main engine brakes for 6 minutes. Apollo 11 is captured by the Moon and orbits it every 2 hours.
Eagle senkt sich aus 15 km Höhe. Armstro: Eagle descends from an altitude of 15 km. Armstrong takes over manually because the computer is heading towards a boulder field – at landing, only seconds of fuel remain.
20:17:40 UTC: Landung im Meer der Ruhe (: 20:17:40 UTC: Landing in the Sea of Tranquility (0.67° N, 23.47° E). The Earth stands high above the horizon – from the landing site, it hardly moves across the sky.
02:56 UTC: „That's one small step for ma: 02:56 UTC: "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." 600 million people are watching live. Armstrong and Aldrin collect 21.5 kg of Moon rock.
Die Aufstiegsstufe startet, die Abstiegs: The ascent stage starts, the descent stage remains as a launch pad. After 7 minutes, Eagle is in orbit and later docks with Columbia.
Wieder hinter dem Mond zündet das Triebw: Again behind the Moon, the engine ignites: Apollo 11 leaves the Moon and falls back to Earth for two and a half days.
Mit 11 km/s trifft die Kapsel auf die At: At 11 km/s, the capsule hits the atmosphere. The heat shield glows at 2,700 °C, the crew experiences 6.5 g.
In 254 km Höhe über der Rückseite – 400: At an altitude of 254 km over the far side – 400,171 km from Earth: Record for the greatest distance humans have ever been from Earth. The Moon's gravity redirects the spacecraft toward Earth.
Mit improvisierten CO₂-Filtern aus Pappe: They survive with improvised CO2 filters made of cardboard and tape. The capsule is lifted back up just in time.
Alle drei Astronauten kehren unversehrt: All three astronauts return unharmed – "a successful failure".
Der unbemannte Testflug des Orion-Raumsc: The unmanned test flight of the Orion spacecraft on the SLS rocket – preparation for the return of humans to the Moon. Orion flew into a wide, "retrograde" orbit around the Moon (DRO) and returned after 25 days.
06:47 UTC: Die stärkste Rakete seit der: 06:47 UTC: The most powerful rocket since the Saturn V lifts off at night in Florida – 8.8 million pounds of thrust.
Die Oberstufe ICPS schickt Orion zum Mon: The ICPS upper stage sends Orion to the Moon. On board: three dummies with radiation meters.
Rund 70 000 km über dem Mond, entgegen s: Around 70,000 km above the Moon, opposite its orbital direction – a very stable orbit that costs hardly any fuel. On 11/28, Orion reaches a distance of 432,210 km from Earth: a record for a manned spacecraft.
Erstmals ein „Hüpf-Eintritt“: Orion tauc: For the first time a “skip entry”: Orion dives into the atmosphere, rises again and dives again. The heat shield reaches 2,800 °C.
Gestartet 16 Tage nach Voyager 2, aber a: Launched 16 days after Voyager 2, but on a faster orbit: It reached Jupiter and Saturn first. After Saturn's moon Titan, it left the planetary plane to the north – today it is the farthest object that humans have built.
Eine Titan-IIIE/Centaur bringt die 722 k: A Titan-IIIE/Centaur puts the 722 kg heavy probe on its way. The planets are favorably aligned as only every 175 years.
Aus 11,7 Mio. km nimmt Voyager 1 das ers: At 11.7 million km, Voyager 1 takes the first photo showing Earth and Moon together as crescents.
Am 5. März 1979 fliegt Voyager 1 in 349: On March 5, 1979, Voyager 1 flies past at a distance of 349,000 km. Discovered: active volcanoes on Io – the first evidence of volcanism outside of Earth – and a thin ring around Jupiter.
Voyager 1 fliegt dicht an Titan vorbei u: Voyager 1 flies close to Titan and sees only orange haze. The trajectory to Titan flings it out of the plane of the planets – Pluto is no longer reachable this way.
Aus 6 Mrd. km dreht sich die Kamera ein: At 6 billion km, the camera turns for the last time: Earth is a faint blue dot, smaller than a pixel. Carl Sagan: “That's here. That's home. That's us.”
In 121 AE überquert Voyager 1 die Heliop: In 121 AU, Voyager 1 crosses the heliopause: The solar wind ends, and the probe measures the denser plasma between the stars.
Die „Grand Tour“: als einzige Sonde an a: The “Grand Tour”: as the only probe to pass all four giant planets. Each flyby redirected it using the planet's gravity to the next one (swing-by) – thus the journey to Neptune took 12 instead of 30 years.
Voyager 2 startet zuerst – auf der langs: Voyager 2 starts first – on the slower orbit that keeps the path to Uranus and Neptune open.
Juli 1979: Bilder von Europas Rissen und: July 1979: images of Europa's cracks and Ganymede's furrows. Jupiter's gravity accelerates Voyager 2 towards Saturn.
August 1981: Speichen in den Ringen, Stü: August 1981: spokes in the rings, storms and the moons Enceladus and Tethys.
Januar 1986: der einzige Besuch bei Uran: January 1986: the only visit to Uranus. Ten new moons, two new rings and Miranda's crazy landscape.
August 1989: 4 950 km über Neptuns Nordp: August 1989: 4,950 km over Neptune's North Pole – the closest flyby of the mission. The Great Dark Spot and the nitrogen geysers on Triton.
Die schnellste Sonde beim Start (16,3 km: The fastest probe at launch (16.3 km/s): past the Moon in 9 hours, at Jupiter after 13 months, at Pluto after 9.5 years.
Eine Atlas V mit fünf Zusatzraketen und: An Atlas V with five solid rocket boosters and a third stage gives New Horizons the highest launch velocity of all time.
Der Vorbeiflug an Jupiter spart 3 Jahre: The flyby of Jupiter saves 3 years of flight time – and delivers films of the volcanic eruption Tvashtar on Io.
14. Juli 2015, 12 500 km über der Oberfl: July 14, 2015, 12,500 km above the surface: the heart of nitrogen ice, icebergs, blue haze layers. The data takes 16 months to reach Earth.
Neujahr 2019: der fernste je besuchte Kö: New Year 2019: the farthest ever visited body, an untouched “snowman” from the formation time of the solar system.
Sieben Jahre Anflug mit vier Schwung-Man: Seven years of approach with four gravity assists (Venus, Venus, Earth, Jupiter), then 13 years in the Saturn system. The Huygens lander landed on Titan. In the end, Cassini intentionally crashed into Saturn to avoid contaminating the moons Enceladus and Titan.
Mit 5,6 Tonnen eine der schwersten Plane: With 5.6 tons, one of the heaviest planetary probes. No rocket was sufficient for the direct path to Saturn – so gravity assists were used.
Gemeinsame Beobachtungen mit der Sonde G: Joint observations with the Galileo probe, which is currently orbiting Jupiter.
Durch eine Lücke in den Ringen hindurch: Through a gap in the rings, the engine fires for 96 minutes: Cassini is captured by Saturn.
Die europäische Kapsel schwebt 2,5 Stund: The European capsule floats for 2.5 hours on a parachute through the haze and lands on frozen ground with water ice pebbles – the farthest landing of all time.
Nach 22 Tauchgängen zwischen Saturn und: After 22 dives between Saturn and its rings, Cassini plunges into the atmosphere on 09/15/2017 and transmits measurements until the very end.
Zehn Jahre Anflug mit drei Erd- und eine: Ten years of approach with three Earth flybys and one Mars flyby, then over two years accompanying comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko. The Philae lander was the first device to land on a comet.
Eine Ariane 5 startet in Französisch-Gua: An Ariane 5 launches in French Guiana. Rosetta is named after the Rosetta Stone – it is intended to help decode the formation of the solar system.
Nur 250 km über der Oberfläche, 24 Minut: Only 250 km above the surface, 24 minutes in the Mars shadow without solar power – a risky maneuver.
Nach 6,4 Milliarden km erreicht Rosetta: After 6.4 billion km, Rosetta reaches the 4 km large comet – shaped like a rubber duck.
Die Harpunen zünden nicht, Philae hüpft: The harpoons do not fire, Philae jumps twice over the surface and remains in the shadow of a cliff – but measures for 57 hours.
Der Komet ist der Sonne am nächsten (1,2: The comet is closest to the Sun (1.24 AU) and most active: gas and dust fountains shoot out from the surface.
Am Ende sinkt Rosetta langsam auf den Ko: In the end, Rosetta slowly descends onto the comet and transmits images until touchdown.
Der Rover sucht im Jezero-Krater, einem: The rover searches in the Jezero Crater, a former river delta, for traces of past life and collects rock samples for later retrieval. On board: the Ingenuity helicopter – the first powered flight on another planet.
Eine Atlas V schickt den 1 Tonne schwere: An Atlas V sends the 1 tonne heavy rover on a 7 month long Hohmann-like orbit to Mars.
Auf einer Halb-Ellipse um die Sonne: Abf: On a semi-ellipse around the Sun: departure when Earth is ahead of the orbit, arrival when Mars is exactly there.
Mit 20 000 km/h in die Marsatmosphäre, H: At 20,000 km/h into the Martian atmosphere, heat shield, supersonic parachute, radar and finally the sky crane, which lowers the rover on cables – all automatic, because radio takes 11 minutes to Earth.
18.02.2021, 20:55 UTC. Am 19.04.2021 fli: 02/18/2021, 20:55 UTC. On 04/19/2021, Ingenuity flies for 39 seconds – the Wright Brothers moment on Mars.
Start am ersten Weihnachtstag 2021, dann: Start on the first day of Christmas 2021, then a one-month flight to the Lagrange point L2 – and along the way, the most difficult deployment maneuver in spaceflight.
So präzise, dass Webb Treibstoff für wei: So precise that Webb has fuel left for well over 10 instead of 5 years.
Sonnenschild (Tennisplatz-groß, 5 Lagen: Sunshield (tennis court-sized, 5 layers thinner than a hair) and the 6.5-m mirror made of 18 gilded segments unfold – 344 individual steps, all of which had to succeed.
1,5 Mio. km hinter der Erde kreist Webb: 1.5 million km behind the Earth, Webb orbits L2 in a halo orbit. Sun, Earth and Moon are always on the same side – the mirror cools down to −233 °C.
Die Leistung verteilt sich auf eine Kuge: The power is distributed over a sphere with radius d – double the distance, a quarter of the light. Therefore, it is 900 times darker at Neptune than at us.
Der Drehimpuls bleibt erhalten. Darum is: Angular momentum is conserved. Therefore, a body is fast near the central body and slow far away – the colored areas above are all equal in size and are covered in equal times.
Kepler fand T² ∝ a³ an den Planeten; New: Kepler found T² ∝ a³ on the planets; Newton showed why: gravity ∝ 1/r². With the formula, one weighs celestial bodies – from the orbital period of a Moon, the mass of the planet follows.
Die sparsamste Bahn zwischen zwei Kreisb: The most economical orbit between two circular orbits: a half ellipse that touches both. This (or almost this) is how probes fly to Mars or Venus – therefore, a launch window opens only every few years.
So lange dauert es, bis Erde, Sonne und: This is how long it takes until Earth, Sun, and the body are aligned again – e.g., from one Mars opposition to the next or from launch window to launch window.
What we see is always the past. Radio commands to probes take just as long – therefore, Mars rovers land fully automatically.
Die Sonne enthält 99,86 % der Masse des: The Sun contains 99.86 % of the mass of the solar system. In its core, it fuses around 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium every second – 4 million tons of which are converted into light. A photon takes between 10,000 and 170,000 years to travel from the core to the surface, depending on the calculation, and only 8 minutes 20 seconds from there to Earth.
Der kleinste und sonnennächste Planet. M: The smallest and closest planet to the Sun. Mercury rotates in a 3:2 resonance: three rotations for every two orbits – a solar day there lasts 176 Earth days. Without an atmosphere, the temperature fluctuates between 430 °C during the day and −180 °C at night. Its iron core fills about 85 % of its radius.
Fast so groß wie die Erde, aber eine Höl: Almost as large as Earth, but a hell: 92 bar of carbon dioxide create a greenhouse effect of 465 °C – hotter than on Mercury. Clouds of sulfuric acid completely shroud the surface and race around the planet in 4 days (superrotation), while Venus itself rotates backwards in 243 days.
Der einzige bekannte Ort mit Leben. Flüs: The only known place with life. Liquid water covers 71 % of the surface; the magnetic field and the atmosphere protect against solar wind and radiation. The large Moon stabilizes the axial tilt of 23.4° – that is why there are reliable seasons.
Der Rote Planet verdankt seine Farbe Eis: The Red Planet owes its color to iron oxide – rust – in the dust. Here stands Olympus Mons, with 22 km the highest volcano in the solar system, and the rift system Valles Marineris, as long as the USA is wide. Water used to flow on Mars; today it is frozen in the polar caps and in the ground.
Jupiter ist schwerer als alle anderen Pl: Jupiter is heavier than all other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm, larger than Earth, that has been raging for at least 190 years. With 10 hours it rotates the fastest of all planets and is consequently visibly flattened. Its magnetic field is the largest structure in the solar system.
Uranus liegt auf der Seite: Seine Achse: Uranus lies on its side: Its axis is tilted by 98°, presumably after a massive collision. Thus, each pole has 42 years of day and 42 years of night. Methane in the atmosphere absorbs red light and colors it pale blue-green. It has 13 dark, narrow rings.
Neptun wurde 1846 nicht durch Beobachtun: Neptune was discovered in 1846 not by observation, but by calculation – from perturbations of Uranus's orbit. Here, the fastest winds of the solar system blow at over 2,000 km/h. It radiates 2.6 times more energy than it receives from the Sun. One orbit takes 165 years – only in 2011 has it orbited the Sun once since its discovery.
Bis 2006 der neunte Planet. 2015 flog Ne: Until 2006 the ninth planet. In 2015, New Horizons flew by and showed a surprisingly lively world: a heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice (Tombaugh Regio), mountains of water ice, and a thin, blue haze. Pluto and Charon always show each other the same side.
Das größte Objekt im Asteroidengürtel –: The largest object in the asteroid belt – one third of its total mass. The Dawn spacecraft found bright spots of salts (sodium carbonate) in the Occator crater, remains of salty water from the interior. Beneath the crust, there could still be brine today.
Fast genauso groß wie Pluto, aber 27 % s: Almost as large as Pluto, but 27% heavier – its discovery in 2005 led to the new definition of a planet. Eris is one of the brightest objects in the solar system: Its methane ice reflects 96% of the light. Currently, it is almost three times as far away as Pluto.
Haumea dreht sich in nur 3,9 Stunden ein: Haumea rotates once around itself in just 3.9 hours – so fast that it is stretched into an ellipsoid, almost twice as long as it is thick. In 2017, a ring around it was discovered during an occultation.
Ein rötlicher, heller Eiszwerg, benannt: A reddish, bright icy dwarf, named after the creator god of the Rapa Nui. Its surface is covered with methane and ethane ice.
Der einzige Mond mit dichter Atmosphäre: The only moon with a dense atmosphere – 1.5 times as much pressure as on Earth, mainly nitrogen. Orange smog from organic molecules hides the surface. There, it rains methane, and there are rivers, lakes, and seas of liquid hydrocarbons. In 2005, the Huygens probe landed; in 2034, the Dragonfly drone is expected to arrive.
Zweifarbig wie Yin und Yang: Die vorausl: Two-colored like Yin and Yang: the leading side is black as coal, the trailing side bright as snow. A 13 km high wall runs exactly along the equator.
Ein eingefangener Kleinkörper aus dem äu: A captured small body from the outer solar system on a retrograde orbit. Its dust forms a huge, barely visible ring.
Triton umläuft Neptun rückwärts – ein ei: Triton orbits Neptune backwards – a captured object from the Kuiper Belt. Nitrogen geysers shoot 8 km high; the surface looks like a melon rind. Tides are slowly pulling it inward: In 3.6 billion years, it will be torn apart and become a ring.
Halb so groß wie Pluto – das Paar umkrei: Half as large as Pluto – the pair orbits a center of mass outside of Pluto and is considered by some as a double dwarf planet. The reddish north pole (Mordor Macula) is colored by methane escaping from Pluto and freezing on Charon.
Das „Quietscheentchen“: Die Sonde Rosett: The "Squeaky Toy": The Rosetta probe accompanied the comet from 2014–2016, the Philae lander was the first to land on a comet nucleus. The probe found amino acids and oxygen.
Der „Große Komet von 1997“ war 18 Monate: The "Great Comet of 1997" was visible to the naked eye for 18 months – a record. Its nucleus is unusually large at around 60 km. It will not return for about 2,500 years.
Der helle Komet vom Oktober 2024 mit Geg: The bright comet from October 2024 with an anti-tail. Its orbit is slightly hyperbolic – it is leaving the solar system forever.
Ein „Felskomet“: Er kommt der Sonne bis: A "rock comet": It comes as close as 0.14 AU to the Sun, becomes 750 °C hot and crumbles. Its dust produces the Geminids in December.
The farthest human-made object. Voyager 1 visited Jupiter and Saturn and crossed the heliopause in 2012 – the boundary to interstellar space. The radio signals take almost a day to reach Earth. On board: the Golden Record with greetings from humanity.
Die einzige Sonde, die Uranus (1986) und: The only probe that visited Uranus (1986) and Neptune (1989). In interstellar space since 2018.
Fliegt durch die Sonnenkorona: Im Perihe: Flies through the solar corona: At perihelion only 6.2 million km above the Sun's surface at 192 km/s – the fastest ever built object. A carbon heat shield withstands 1,400 °C, behind which it remains at room temperature.
Das größte Weltraumteleskop kreist 1,5 M: The largest space telescope orbits 1.5 million km behind the Earth around the Lagrange point L2, where Sun, Earth and Moon always stand on the same side of its sunshield. It observes the first galaxies after the Big Bang in infrared.
Die Internationale Raumstation umrundet: The International Space Station orbits the Earth in 92 minutes – 16 times a day. Humans have been living on board constantly since November 2000.
Mitte August kreuzt die Erde die Staubsp: In mid-August, Earth crosses the dust trail of Swift-Tuttle. The grains hit the atmosphere at 59 km/s and incinerate at an altitude of 100 km. Up to 100 shooting stars per hour – the most popular meteor shower of the year.
Mitte November. Schnellste Meteore überh: In mid-November. Fastest meteors ever (71 km/s), because Earth meets the stream head-on. Meteor storms are possible every 33 years.
Staub des Halleyschen Kometen, im Oktobe: Dust from Halley's Comet in October. The trail hits Earth's orbit twice; the Eta Aquariids are created as a result in May.
